text: The warehouse is built — now comes the part that decides whether the migration succeeds: how the organization stops depending on the old sources and starts depending on this one.
Big-bang cutover repoints everything at once — fast, but no partial-failure mode. Phased, parallel-run cutover moves consumers over one report at a time, as each is validated — lower blast radius.

A reconciliation query asks the same business question of both warehouses, daily, and flags any variance. Zero rows across the full parallel-run window is the actual bar for calling a report validated.

A rollback plan answers what the trigger is, what the mechanism is, and how long the old source stays alive — decided before cutover starts, not during an incident. Cutover for a report is 'go' only when reconciliation shows zero unexplained variance for the full agreed window.
A phased cutover, validated by a query that runs the whole way through, with a rollback plan agreed in advance. Next up: closing out Project 2 with an honest retrospective.
